summary: Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of British Columbia. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and taught religious studies at Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, earning a master's at Seabury-Western Theological Seminary. He was Episcopal chaplain at Northwestern University (1944–1950), a dozent at the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957), and a Harvard fellow (1962–1964).

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who completed his MA at the University of Edinburgh and his Ph.D. at the University of Pittsburgh. He was assistant professor at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became emeritus professor at Toronto in 1986.

Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning his PhD from the University of Cambridge around 2008–2013. He became Assistant Professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2016) and a Research Associate at SOAS (attested 2019).

Albert Debrunner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel and Ferdinand Sommer. His posts included Privatdozent at Zurich (~1917–1918), professor at Greifswald (1918), Dozent at Jena (1925–1935), and professor at Bern (1920, 1935).

Albert Grünwedel was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology who earned his Dr. phil. at Munich under Michael Bernays and Ernst Kuhn. He served at the Berlin Ethnological Museum (1881–1921, becoming director) and held an honorary professorship at Berlin (1891).

Albert Hoefer was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Berlin. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald from roughly 1840 to 1883, including an extraordinary professorship (1847–1880).
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from around 1925 to 1929. He subsequently held a post at Novartis from circa 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a specialist in sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker. He served at the Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019).
Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva and under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1903 to 1945.

Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his habilitation at Freiburg. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1895), University of Marburg (1901), and University of Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Venn Dicey studied at King's College School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at the University of Oxford in 1882 and served at the London School of Economics from circa 1896 to 1899.

Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, earning his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He was Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2013) before joining the University of Arizona as department head in 2013.

Albion Moonlight Butters is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he earned his Ph.D. under Robert A. F. Thurman.

Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from Breslau and Berlin, studying under Christian Lassen. He spent his career at the University of Berlin as Privatdozent and Extraordinarius between 1848 and 1901.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist and philosopher who completed his Dr. phil. at Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and directed the Nepal Research Centre and Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs. In 2019, he held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and the Singapore University of Technology and Design.

Alessandro Graheli is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. In 2022, he was attested as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Alex McKay is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology who earned his PhD from SOAS in 1995. He has held fellowships at SOAS, University College London, and the International Institute for Asian Studies.
